name: Confirm and affirm trades with brokers and counterparties
summary: Before a trade can settle, the fund and the broker or counterparty must agree its details. Trade support sends each allocation to DTCC's Central Trade Manager, where it is matched automatically against the broker's confirmation, confirms FX and money market trades through electronic matching, checks listed futures against the clearing broker's file and confirms OTC derivatives on an electronic platform or by signed long-form confirmation. Most trades match without anyone touching them; analysts work the mismatches, which are mostly late or wrong broker details, before the noon T+1 matching deadline in Canada and the 11:30 a.m. T+1 affirmation cut-off in the U.S. Paper derivative confirmations take days and need chasing and two signatures.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager whose middle office matches trades through DTCC CTM and electronic FX and derivative confirmation services, with SimCorp Dimension as book of record.
baseline.notes: Volume follows the organisation file estimate of about 40,000 allocations a month, the same allocations that booking produces. Canada and the U.S. settled on T+2 throughout the period.

trigger: A booked trade ticket is released from booking, or a broker or counterparty confirmation arrives for a trade.
end_state: The trade is matched and affirmed, or its confirmation signed, and it is released to settlement; or it is cancelled because neither side recognises it.

volume.seasonality: Follows trading volume, with an evening peak after the North American close and a morning peak for overnight Asian and European exceptions.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate (process mkt-confirm-affirm).

Confirmation and affirmation share of the 26 trade support analysts. Loaded cost from the organisation file; Job Bank NOC 11109 Toronto median C$34.62 an hour before incentives, benefits and overhead.
Exception approvals, OTC paper confirmations and deadline reviews.

steps.name: Trade ticket enters the confirmation queue
steps.description: A booked and enriched allocation arrives from booking, or an unexpected broker or counterparty confirmation arrives first and is linked to its trade. The queue routes it by product: broker-executed equities and bonds to CTM, FX and money market trades to electronic confirmation matching, listed futures and options to the clearing broker check, and OTC derivatives to bilateral confirmation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: equity, ETF or bond trade with a broker

evidence.note: Asset classes handled (listed equities, fixed income and repo, money market, FX, securities lending) from fund_posting; product mix by allocation is an author estimate.

steps.name: Send the allocation to CTM
steps.description: SimCorp or the OMS sends the account-level allocation (security, side, quantity, price, commission, settlement date and account SSIs) to DTCC's Central Trade Manager for the executing broker.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Allocation details go to the executing broker to start confirmation (dtcc_auto, dtcc_ctm).

steps.name: Broker books the allocation and submits its confirmation
steps.description: The executing broker's middle office books the allocation in its own system and submits the trade-level confirmation (price, commission, fees, net amount, settlement date and instructions) to CTM. Brokers working through the post-close peak, and Asian brokers overnight, can take hours.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Confirmation starts only after allocation and most allocations come after the close (t1report). Wait range is an author estimate.

steps.name: CTM matches allocation and confirmation
steps.description: CTM compares the fund's allocation with the broker's confirmation field by field within agreed tolerances on price, commission and net amount. A match is agreed automatically; otherwise the trade appears as mismatched or unmatched on both parties' dashboards.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: CTM central matching (dtcc_ctm). Same-day affirmation was 73% of U.S. institutional trades at the end of January 2024 (sifma_aar); the 86% first-pass match rate assumed for a large, automated investor is an author estimate.

steps.name: Review a CTM exception
steps.description: The analyst opens the CTM exception dashboard, compares the mismatched fields (commission, net amount, settlement date, SSI, account, quantity) with the booking and the trader's execution, and decides which side is wrong.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: our booking or allocation is wrong
price or commission disputed, trader needed

evidence.note: Late or wrong broker details cause most exceptions (organisation file description); inaccurate SSIs are a leading cause of exceptions (dtcc_alert). Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Ask the broker to correct its confirmation
steps.description: The analyst adds a comment in CTM and emails or calls the broker's middle office with the correct details and the deadline.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Broker corrects and resubmits
steps.description: The broker cancels and replaces its confirmation in CTM. Busy or overseas brokers may not act until their next business morning.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: still unmatched on the morning of T+1

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Correct our booking and resend the allocation
steps.description: The analyst amends the trade in SimCorp (wrong account, commission or settlement detail), cancels the allocation in CTM and sends the corrected one.

error.defect_description: Amendment introduces another error.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Second person approves the amendment
steps.description: A senior associate checks the amendment against the trader's execution and approves it before the corrected allocation is released to CTM.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Maker-checker on trade amendments: trades recorded accurately (SOC 1 baseline trading objective)

evidence.note: Trades authorised and recorded accurately (sifma_soc).

steps.name: Trader settles a price or commission dispute
steps.description: The analyst asks the trader to confirm the agreed price or commission; the trader checks the execution record and agrees the correct figure with the broker's desk, or confirms the trade is not ours.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Accept a small difference and force-match
steps.description: A senior associate reviews a difference such as commission rounding or a few cents on the net amount, confirms it is within the force-match authority and matches the trade, recording the reason.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Matching tolerance and force-match authority in the investment operations procedures

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Affirm the matched trade and notify settlement
steps.description: Once the match is agreed the trade is affirmed automatically and the settlement details are sent onward: to the depository's affirmation service for U.S. trades, to CDS for Canadian trades, and to the custodian.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: NI 24-101 institutional trade matching: match as soon as practical and by noon on T+1 (trade-matching statement given to dealers); 11:30 AM ET T+1 affirmation cut-off in the U.S. under T+2

evidence.note: Noon T+1 matching deadline and 90% exception threshold (ni24101); 11:30 AM ET T+1 affirmation deadline (t1report, dtcc_auto).

steps.name: Match the FX or money market confirmation
steps.description: SimCorp sends the fund's confirmation message for the FX or money market trade and the matching service compares it with the counterparty's message on currency pair, amounts, rate, value date and settlement instructions.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: FX Global Code principle 46: confirm trades as soon as practicable using automated confirmation matching

evidence.note: Principles 46 to 48 on prompt, automated confirmation and resolving discrepancies (fxgc). Match rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate an unmatched FX or money market confirmation
steps.description: The analyst compares the two confirmations with the booking, identifies the wrong field (often value date, amount or SSI) and contacts the counterparty's confirmation desk.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: FX Global Code principle 48: identify and resolve confirmation discrepancies as soon as practicable

evidence.note: Principle 48 (fxgc); time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Counterparty corrects or confirms
steps.description: The counterparty's confirmation desk checks its own booking, then amends and resends its confirmation message or replies that the fund's record is the one that is wrong.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: trader needed to agree the terms

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check the clearing broker's trade file
steps.description: Listed futures and options are not confirmed bilaterally. Each evening or next morning the analyst compares booked trades with the clearing broker's trade and give-up file by contract, quantity, price and account.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Trades recorded accurately and completely (SOC 1 baseline trading objective)

next.condition: missing give-up, wrong account or price

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice for exchange-traded derivatives.

steps.name: Resolve a futures give-up or clearing break
steps.description: The analyst works with the executing and clearing brokers to fix a missing or misallocated give-up, or with the trader when the price differs, and confirms the corrected position.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Affirm the OTC derivative on the electronic confirmation platform
steps.description: For swaps and other standard OTC derivatives the counterparty submits the trade on the electronic confirmation platform; the analyst checks the economic terms (notional, dates, rates, fixed and floating legs, fees) against the booking and affirms. Non-standard trades go to paper confirmation instead.
outputs: affirmed OTC trade or paper route

error.defect_description: Economic term difference overlooked at affirmation.

control.basis: Derivatives confirmation policy: every OTC trade confirmed with the counterparty under the ISDA master agreement

next.condition: electronic confirmation agrees and is affirmed
electronic confirmation differs from the booking
non-electronic trade: wait for a paper confirmation

evidence.note: 83% of electronically eligible interest rate derivative events were confirmed electronically in 2011 and 11% of trade records contained errors (isda_obs). Shares here are author estimates for 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Wait for the counterparty's long-form confirmation
steps.description: For non-standard derivatives the counterparty drafts a long-form confirmation and sends it as a PDF or document, often several business days after the trade.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: ISDA tracks confirmations outstanding in business days and aged over 30 and 90 days (isda_obs); durations are author estimates.

steps.name: Chase an overdue confirmation
steps.description: The analyst emails and calls the counterparty's documentation team about confirmations outstanding beyond the target and records the item on the aged confirmations report.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Review the long-form confirmation
steps.description: A senior associate compares the confirmation line by line with the booking, the trader's term sheet and the ISDA master agreement and credit support annex, and asks Legal about non-standard language.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Derivatives confirmation policy and ISDA documentation standards

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Resolve an OTC confirmation discrepancy
steps.description: The senior associate raises the difference with the counterparty and, when the economics are in doubt, with the trader or portfolio manager, until both sides agree the terms and a corrected confirmation is issued.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Authorised signatories sign the confirmation
steps.description: Two authorised signatories, the trade support director and another officer on the signing list, sign the confirmation and it is returned to the counterparty and filed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Signing authority policy: two authorised signatories on confirmations

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Review trades unmatched at the deadline
steps.description: Each morning of T+1 a senior associate goes through the report of trades still unmatched before the noon matching deadline and the custodian's instruction cut-offs, assigns owners and escalates brokers that are repeatedly late.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: NI 24-101 matching by noon on T+1 and monitoring of other trade-matching parties' performance (Companion Policy 24-101CP)

evidence.note: Noon T+1 deadline, 90% threshold and dealer monitoring of other parties (ni24101); T+2 from September 5, 2017 with matching on T+1 (cibcm_t2).

steps.name: Warn settlements about a late-matching trade
steps.description: The settlement analyst is told which trades will be instructed late, checks the custodian's market deadline and prepares the instruction or a pre-advice so the trade can still settle on time.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Settlements team works to market deadlines with brokers and custodians (fund_posting).

steps.name: Release the confirmed trade to settlement
steps.description: The matched, affirmed or signed trade is marked confirmed in SimCorp and becomes eligible for settlement instruction to the custodian.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Matched and agreed trades move into settlement (dtcc_auto).

exceptions.name: Broker detail wrong in CTM
exceptions.description: The broker's commission, net amount, settlement date or SSI differs; the broker cancels and resubmits, sometimes not until the next morning.

exceptions.name: Our booking wrong
exceptions.description: The fund's allocation, account or commission is wrong and is amended under maker-checker before resending.

exceptions.name: Unmatched at the T+1 deadline
exceptions.description: The trade is still unmatched on the morning of T+1; it is escalated and settlements pre-advise the custodian.

exceptions.name: Unmatched FX or money market confirmation
exceptions.description: Value date, amount or SSI differs between the two confirmations.

exceptions.name: Paper OTC confirmation
exceptions.description: Non-standard derivatives need a long-form confirmation that arrives days later, is chased, reviewed and signed by two signatories.

exceptions.name: Trade not recognised
exceptions.description: Neither the trader nor the broker recognises the trade and it is cancelled.

benchmarks.population: Author estimate anchored on Canadian and U.S. matching rules under T+2

benchmarks.unit: share of DAP/RAP trades by value and volume
benchmarks.population: Canadian registered dealers and advisers under NI 24-101

evidence.note: Quarterly exception report required below 90%, under moratorium from July 1, 2020.

benchmarks.unit: share of institutional trades affirmed by 9 PM ET on trade date
benchmarks.population: U.S. institutional trades, end of January 2024 (still T+2)

evidence.note: Rose to nearly 95% after the move to T+1 in May 2024; rates in 2019 to 2022 were likely lower.
Up from 61% in 2009.

pain_points.description: Broker confirmations arrive late in the evening after the close, so exceptions are worked late or the next morning against the noon T+1 deadline.

evidence.note: Allocations mostly after the close (t1report); noon T+1 deadline (ni24101).

pain_points.description: Most mismatches come from brokers' wrong commissions, net amounts or settlement instructions, which the fund can only chase.

evidence.note: Inaccurate SSI data is a leading cause of trade exceptions (dtcc_alert).

pain_points.description: Non-standard OTC derivatives still rely on paper confirmations that take days, need chasing and two signatures, and stay on aged reports.

evidence.note: Confirmations outstanding measured in business days (isda_obs).

sources.title: Associate, Cash, Collateral & Settlements Operations (job posting)
sources.supports: Investment Operations settlements team: affirmation, confirmation and settlement of listed equities, fixed income and repo, money market, FX and securities lending; relationships with brokers, custodians and prime brokers; Bloomberg, SimCorp and affirmation and matching platforms; settlement on time in line with market deadlines and internal policy

sources.title: Accelerating the U.S. Securities Settlement Cycle to T+1
sources.supports: About 20% of institutional allocations occur during the trading day and 80% after the close; affirmation deadline 11:30 AM ET on T+1 under T+2; confirmation and affirmation can only start once allocations are complete; causes of settlement errors and fails include missing or incorrect SSIs, stale reference data, recalls and cancel and rebill

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Baseline SOC 1 control objectives: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded accurately, completely and timely; block orders allocated according to management methodologies and allocations approved; new securities authorised and processed accurately; cash and positions reconciled to custodians

sources.title: FX Global Code (updated December 2024; first published 2017)
sources.supports: Principles 46 to 55: confirm trades as soon as practicable using automated matching; review, affirm and allocate block transactions as soon as practicable; resolve confirmation and settlement discrepancies; measure settlement risk and use PVP where practicable; use standard settlement instructions; request direct payments; reconcile accounts and submit compensation claims in a timely manner

sources.title: ALERT: standing settlement instruction platform
sources.supports: Industry's largest SSI database, shared automatically with counterparties; enrichment with CTM supports straight-through processing; 57% of ALERT SSIs managed by custodians and prime brokers; outdated, incomplete or inaccurate SSI data is a leading cause of trade exceptions and settlement failure

sources.title: Central Trade Manager (CTM)
sources.supports: Central matching platform automating allocation, confirmation and matching for equities, fixed income and money markets; Match to Instruct workflow with ALERT and TradeSuite ID; optional SSI enrichment; dashboards with same-day match agreed rates

sources.title: Why Automation is Pivotal to Prepare for T+1 in U.S.
sources.supports: Workflow of allocation, confirmation and affirmation; centrally matched trades can be affirmed and instructed automatically; affirmation deadline 11:30 AM ET on T+1; near 100% affirmation by 9 PM on trade date for automated workflows

sources.title: SIFMA, ICI and DTCC Release T+1 After Action Report (press release)
sources.supports: Same-day affirmation by 9 PM ET was 73% at the end of January 2024 under T+2 and nearly 95% after T+1; average CNS fail rate 2.12% and DTC non-CNS fail rate 3.31% in July 2024, consistent with T+2 averages

sources.title: CSA Notice and Request for Comment: Proposed Amendments to NI 24-101 Institutional Trade Matching and Settlement
sources.supports: NI 24-101 in force since 2007; dealers and advisers trading DAP/RAP for institutional investors must have policies to match trades as soon as practical and by noon on T+1; quarterly exception report if fewer than 90% of trades by value and volume match by the deadline (moratorium from July 1, 2020); CDS and matching utilities report matching data; trade-matching agreements or statements with institutional clients; Companion Policy guidance on best practices and monitoring other parties

sources.title: Shortening the Settlement Cycle: Final CSA Amendments to NI 24-101
sources.supports: Canadian move to T+2 on September 5, 2017 in line with the U.S.; extended noon T+2 matching deadline for non-North-American trades repealed so parties match on T+1

sources.title: ISDA Operations Benchmarking Survey 2011
sources.supports: Interest rate derivative trade records containing errors 18% (2009), 14% (2010), 11% (2011), most attributable to the front office; counterparty name and payment dates are top error sources; 83% of electronically eligible interest rate derivative events confirmed electronically in 2011; confirmation backlogs measured in business days outstanding

sources.title: Wages: Credit Counsellor and other financial officers (NOC 11109) in the Toronto Region
sources.supports: Toronto Region hourly wages for NOC 11109: low 23.00, median 34.62, high 66.46 (2023-2024)

assumptions: Product mix by allocation (68% CTM-matched equities and bonds, 20% FX and money market, 9% listed derivatives, 3% OTC derivatives) is an author estimate.

First-pass CTM match rate of 86% is an author estimate for a large, largely automated investor; the U.S. market-wide same-day affirmation rate was 73% at the end of January 2024 and lower earlier in the T+2 period.

NI 24-101 places the matching obligation on registered dealers and advisers; the fund takes part through trade-matching statements with its dealers and its custodian, so the deadline is treated as fixed by law for the process even though the fund is not the registrant.
The CTM to affirmation link is modelled as automatic once matched, as in DTCC's Match to Instruct workflow; trades in markets without central matching are folded into the CTM path.
Trade support analysts also work on booking and OTC lifecycle events, so their FTE here is a share of the team. Settlements are involved only for late-matching trades.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file; they include incentive pay and an overhead factor of 1.25.
